output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration

Dana, I said I would write this up once I had put my machine through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial, so here is the promised review.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, and picked it up on Tuesday, October 27: six business days, against the ten business days quoted. The estimate was $285 for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning, and a firmware update. The final bill was $310: the original $285, plus $25 for a replacement internal battery. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court.

The completed work was a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, a firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and the battery replacement. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am satisfied that the problem I brought it in for has been addressed.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson. Parking behind the shop is free. Gloria Ruark did the work. She contacted me about the battery after finding it was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity and specifically said she would not replace it without my approval. I approved the additional $25. Asking first matters to me, and $310 strikes me as fair for everything that was done.

The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never received that from anyone before, and it is useful to have a record beyond the invoice.

They supplied a Stenvale Aria 2 loaner, which meant I could keep working. It was not perfect: its tilt arm slipped during a mid-afternoon deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I reported that to Gloria so it would not simply go out to someone else in the same condition. She thanked me and said they would repair the arm.

The real weakness is telephone access. Their phone is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. I called on Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress; it rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria did email me the following day, so I was not left without information for long, but anyone working a Monday docket should understand that they may not be able to reach the shop by phone when a problem arises.

Dana, my bottom line is yes: based on this visit, I would trust Harbor Point with my Aria again, including for a number bar problem like yours. Gloria did good, careful work, communicated in writing, and did not pad the bill. Plan around the limited phone hours and check the loaner before you leave, but neither of those caveats changes my recommendation.
